# EA Audio

Public website: https://ebinaugustin.github.io/ea-audio-website/

EA Analyser: `analyser.html`, Windows Edition 0.8.3, US$5 one-time via https://ko-fi.com/s/d8abc79313. The homepage includes a product announcement. `analyser.css` provides the product page and announcement styles. Screenshots use the existing public Ko-fi product image URLs; disclosure distinguishes interface renders from the actual REAPER screenshot.

Support center: `support.html` offers plugin-specific email bug reports, with Copy report as a fallback. It does not claim to submit or store reports. The account-based chat app is prepared separately in `work/ea-audio-helpdesk` and must have Supabase email authentication connected before it can replace this interim email workflow. No support backend secrets belong in this public repository.

The creator’s message to developers appears first. RoomMatch beta 0.2.3 follows, with direct installer links for Windows x64, Mac Apple Silicon, and Mac Intel.

Release: https://github.com/Ebinaugustin/EA-RoomMatch-Image-to-Reverb/releases/tag/v0.2.3-beta.1

To update downloads, edit `downloads.js` and the corresponding installer anchors and size labels in `index.html`. Bump script query versions after changes. GitHub Pages publishes the main branch automatically.

EA Native Automation: `automation.html`, with a homepage announcement and navigation link. Its ReaPack URL, platform availability and known issues are maintained on that page. Screenshot assets are in `assets/automation/`; the gallery and Copy URL button use `automation.js`.

Optional support: the homepage `#support` section links to [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/ebinaugustin) and UPI ID `ebin.augustin55@oksbi` with no preset amount, plus a Copy ID fallback for desktop. Music links provide another way to support EA Audio. RoomMatch is free and will remain free forever; this promise does not apply to every EA Audio product. Contributions do not unlock RoomMatch downloads.



## 8-bit design

Approved and published on 12 November 2026. The site uses the existing charcoal, ivory and coral palette, self-hosted pixel and monospace fonts, an accessible mobile menu, pixel-art illustrations and direct product descriptions. The developer message is expandable at the top of the homepage. Existing download, purchase, music and support links are preserved.

The new design is in pixel.css and pixel.js; font licences are in assets/fonts/. All four public pages load this theme after their product styles.

Dialogue Alignment Engine: `alignment.html`, free Windows x64 2.0.0-preview, with a homepage announcement, shared navigation link and support-form selection. `alignment.css` provides its page/announcement styles. The actual compiled interface screenshot uses generated audio.

The versioned download in `downloads/dialogue-alignment-engine/2.0.0-preview/` includes VST3/ARA, unsigned AAX Native, documentation, licences and corresponding source. The separate README, validation and licence files are copies from that package. SHA256SUMS.txt verifies the full ZIP. Keep download filenames and checksums in sync when updating; do not silently replace a published version. AAX is unsigned and cannot load in standard retail Pro Tools. Real-host and production-dialogue qualification are pending.

!A MESSAGE TO THE DEVELOPERS. With respect, from Ebin.READ NOTE

First, I want to make something clear: I am not a professional plugin developer or a coder. I’m an audio professional who enjoys experimenting with ideas, exploring new possibilities, and sharing the tools I create along the way.

RoomMatch is free, and will remain free forever. I’m not doing this to compete with commercial developers or to undermine the incredible work they do. Quite the opposite — I have immense respect for the people who dedicate their time, knowledge, creativity, and countless hours of hard work to building audio plugins.

AI has made it easier for people like me to experiment with ideas that might otherwise have remained just ideas. But generating code and building a truly innovative, reliable, and well-engineered plugin are two very different things. Behind great software is a level of understanding, problem-solving, experience, and creativity that deserves recognition.

To the human developers out there: we need you. Your innovations, your expertise, and your passion are what push this industry forward. AI can be a powerful tool, but it is not a replacement for the ingenuity of people who know their craft and dare to build something new.

These plugins are simply my way of experimenting, learning, and sharing something useful with the audio community.

Much respect to every developer who makes the tools we use possible. Keep innovating. The audio world needs you.

A FEW THINGS TO KNOW

RoomMatch
questions.

What is RoomMatch?+

RoomMatch is EA Audio’s first audio plugin: an experimental image-to-reverb tool. Load a room photo, generate an impulse response, and shape its playback with reverb and spatial controls.

Does it recreate the photographed room exactly?+

No. The photo model suggests an acoustic starting point. Room dimensions, materials, and positions are manually adjustable, and the image is not a metric reconstruction or acoustic measurement.

Which formats and platforms are available?+

RoomMatch beta is available for Windows x64, Mac Apple Silicon, and Mac Intel. Each package includes a VST3 plugin and a standalone application.

Does photo analysis need an internet connection?+

The complete packages include the AI model and runtime for offline inference. First-time preparation can take a few minutes. See the release notes for installation details.

How do I install RoomMatch?+

Close your DAW before installing. On Windows, extract the complete ZIP and run Install RoomMatch.cmd. On Mac, choose the PKG for Apple Silicon or Intel. The Mac packages are not Apple notarized. See the release notes for installation details.

LATEST RELEASE / 2.2.15

Version 2.2.15.
Changes.

Version 2.2.15 is now available through ReaPack for Windows x64 and both Intel and Apple Silicon Macs, with the improvements below.

01 / SENDS

Copy Send 1–10

Ten separate commands copy each send slot’s volume, pan and mute automation. Paste matches an existing bus first, then the send slot. It never creates missing sends; unmatched parameters are reported.

02 / PREVIEW

Preview indicators

The whole Preview button blinks green while active; the separate dot is gone. Preview follows across all tracks and Master. Turning it off sets them to Read and removes the global override. Ctrl/Cmd-click retains Preview A/B suspension.

03 / DOCKING

Reveal as you resize

Controls keep their chosen size while the Docker divider reveals more rows or columns. Thin top/bottom docks form a row; narrow side docks form a column. Overflow scrolls instead of shrinking the whole toolbar.

04 / SECTIONS

Keep what you use

Right-click → Show sections lets you show or hide Suspend, Write Enable, Manual Write, Write on Stop and Copy/Paste. Section choices are saved; hiding a section does not change its automation state.

05 / LEGIBILITY

Clearer small controls

Small text and vector icons render at their final size on the pixel grid. The panel reads REAPER 7’s Inter/Inter Medium fonts when present, with system-font fallbacks. Exact 50–200% presets remain available.

06 / SHORTCUTS

104 actions

Separate send-copy and section-visibility actions join the existing commands. Assign your own keys in REAPER’s Main Actions list. The panel also preserves your “Automatically add envelopes when tweaking parameters in automation write modes” preference.

These features are included in the v2.2.15 ReaPack update. Automated checks passed; live Mac REAPER testing and the reported track volume/pan write issues remain open.

WHY I MADE IT

Why I
made it.

Switching from Pro Tools, I wanted a compact automation window that felt familiar in a post session. REAPER’s scripting and extension capabilities made it possible to build one around its own automation system.

THE AUTOMATION WORKFLOW

Preview. Capture.
Write.

Keep the controls you reach for together, then put the actions under your own keyboard shortcuts.

01 / ENABLE

Choose your parameters

Write Enable gates plug-in parameters, track volume/pan/mute and send volume/pan/mute. PAN includes ReaSurround and ReaSurroundPan.

02 / HOLD

Preview & Capture

Hold values in Preview and suspend/resume it for A/B comparison. The whole Preview button blinks green when active. Capture scoped values, or Ctrl/Cmd-click Capture for selected tracks with a blinking indicator.

03 / COMMIT

Write to your range

Five Manual Write ranges and five Write on Stop modes. A successful Manual Write exits Preview. Writing the full session without a time selection asks for confirmation.

04 / REUSE

Copy. Paste. Fill.

Copy All, Copy Pan, or an individual send slot from 1–10. Paste at cursor, stretch to selection, or repeat/fill to selection. Ordinary envelope points are the default; automation items are optional.

05 / MATCH

Keep your routing

Paste automation across tracks using parameter matching. Sends use existing routing: match the bus first, then the send slot. Missing parameters are reported.

06 / CONTROL

Join, match & suspend

Auto Join, Auto Match, track scope and automation modes stay in reach. Suspend bypasses existing envelopes and restores their previous activation when released.

MAKE IT FIT YOUR SESSION

Docking and
panel layouts.

Float the panel, dock it beneath Master or use a shallow horizontal layout. In v2.2.15, dragging the divider reveals fixed-size controls as rows or columns.

ACTUAL USER CAPTURES · EARLIER RELEASE

Theme backgrounds and exposed accent colours carry into the panel. Choose Follow REAPER or five additional panel styles. Rounded buttons, vector icons and press feedback complete the interface.

Right-click for the details

Docking/undocking, Docker selection, themes, size, track scope, automation modes, startup settings, show/hide sections and the running version are available from the panel’s right-click menu.

Auto50%75%100%125%150%175%200%

Floating Auto adapts to the monitor. Docked Auto uses a compact 75% size. Explicit presets stay fixed as the Docker divider reveals more controls; overflow scrolls.

actions.

CURRENT TESTING STATUS

Known issues
and testing.

This is a tool still being tested in live REAPER sessions. Reproducible reports help identify where the host behaves differently.

Track volume and ordinary track pan Manual Write have reported cases of cursor dips/two points instead of the selected-range write, along with unexpected envelope-lane visibility. Recent hotfixes address these paths, but live confirmation remains pending.

If you encounter a problem, include the running version, affected parameter, Preview state, track scope and whether a time selection was present. The engine can write ManualWrite-diagnostics.txt beside engine.lua when verification fails.

Windows native checks and the 104-scenario Lua model suite (1,393 assertions) passed. The Mac universal build, Intel/Apple Silicon model checks and disposable-Mac install/upgrade checks passed. These checks do not verify live REAPER automation or Mac docking/scaling; live platform feedback is still needed. Linux compilation remains pending.

Install the VST3 in REAPER

  1. Download and extract the complete ZIP.
  2. Copy the entire Dialogue Alignment Engine.vst3 folder from the VST3 directory into a VST3 folder scanned by REAPER. Keep its Contents folder intact.
  3. Rescan plug-ins and insert VST3: Dialogue Alignment Engine (Ebin Augustin) on a track.
  4. Select suitable items across your microphone tracks, open the plug-in, and press Capture.

The usual shared Windows folder is C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3. You can also use your own folder and add it to REAPER’s VST scan paths. There is no installer, and the native plug-in does not require the Lua action.

AAX: unsigned developer build

The included AAX bundle will not load in standard retail Pro Tools until the official signing process is completed. It is AAX Native, with no ARA binding, AudioSuite or HDX DSP workflow.

03 / BEFORE YOU START

Know the
current limits.

Use a copy of your session while evaluating this development preview. The included documentation describes each host workflow and its limits.

What does dynamic correction do?+

Dynamic time estimates changing delay across a recording rather than applying one offset to the whole clip. Time + phase adds experimental adaptive spectral phase correction. Results depend on the shared performance and recording conditions; audition them before applying.

Which REAPER items can I capture?+

Whole, normal-rate mono or stereo file takes, without take FX or envelopes, stretch markers, loops, grouping, locks, reversed or section sources, or existing inverted take/track polarity. Capture is limited to 512 MB total and ten minutes per clip. Track effects are outside the source analysis.

How does the ARA workflow differ?+

The VST3 includes an ARA 2 factory and playback/editor integration. Assign the relevant microphone regions through the host’s ARA workflow. In REAPER, use Views → Capture ARA document. Only host-assigned regions are accessible; stretched ARA regions are refused. Host playback and archive round trips still need qualification.

Are my original files changed?+

The REAPER selected-item workflow creates 32-bit float WAV files in the project’s Dialogue Alignment Renders folder. Original media files are not overwritten. Keep the render folder when saving, sharing or moving a project. Revert is available for the current capture session; committed media remains after reopening a project.

What has been tested?+

# Dialogue Alignment Engine 2.0.0 — native development preview

Windows x64 VST3 with ARA 2 support, plus an **unsigned AAX Native development build**. Both embed the audio processor and runtime; the Lua action is not needed to run the plug-in. This is a new native port, not a qualified production release or proof of commercial-equivalent audio quality.

## Install the VST3

Copy the entire `Dialogue Alignment Engine.vst3` **folder** into a VST3 folder scanned by REAPER, then rescan plug-ins. A standard shared location is `C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3`, which may require administrator access. Alternatively, put it in your own plug-in folder and add that folder to REAPER's VST scan paths. Keep the bundle's `Contents` directory intact. Insert **VST3: Dialogue Alignment Engine (Ebin Augustin)** on a track.

The original `Dialogue Alignment Engine.lua` 1.4.5 remains a separate, unchanged fallback. Do not replace that action with the native plug-in files.

## REAPER selected-item workflow

1. Select same-performance audio items on the primary and target microphone tracks.
2. Open the native plug-in and press **Capture**. Choose the primary track.
3. Choose **Dynamic time** or **Time + phase**, the search range and polarity mode. Press **Analyze**. Processing runs on a background worker; the status and moving footer indicator show activity. Analyze becomes Cancel while processing.
4. Use **Original / Aligned** to audition. **Apply** keeps accepted corrections directly, without a confirmation dialog. **Revert** restores the captured sources. Source changes use REAPER undo blocks, keep current item/take colours and selection, and build peaks for the replacement sources.
5. Captured source, position, offset, relevant item/take properties and original file metadata are checked before Apply. Conflicting edits require a new capture. Revert does not overwrite a conflicting source edit. Original media files are not overwritten.

Corrected 32-bit float WAV files are written under the project's `Dialogue Alignment Renders` folder. Include this folder when moving or sharing a project. Retain ever-attached render files for saved projects and Undo/Redo. REAPER-mode Revert is session-local, as in the Lua action; after closing/reopening a project, the corrected media remains part of the project.

Capture supports whole normal-rate mono/stereo file takes, without take FX/envelopes, stretch markers, loops, grouping, locks, reversed/section sources or existing inverted take/track polarity. Track effects are outside the pairwise source analysis. Total captured audio is capped at 512 MB and individual clips at ten minutes. Native host gain/fade interpretation still needs real-session qualification.

## ARA document workflow

The VST3 advertises an ARA factory and playback/editor integration. In an ARA-capable host, enable the plug-in as an ARA extension for all involved microphone tracks/regions, using the host's normal ARA workflow. ARA exposes only regions assigned to its document; inserting an ordinary effect on one unrelated track does not grant access to every project track.

Use **Views > Capture ARA document** to explicitly choose ARA random access in REAPER. In another ARA host, Capture uses its ARA document automatically. The overview includes all assigned regions and track sequences; choose the reference, Analyze, audition and Apply. ARA corrections stay in the model and are serialized through the host's ARA archive rather than replacing project media. Uncommitted ARA previews are staged separately from committed archive data. Model changes after capture invalidate Apply. Host callbacks, archive round trips and audible playback require further REAPER/ARA-host qualification.

ARA regions with unequal playback/modification durations are refused for analysis; render stretched material to normal-rate audio first. Unprocessed ARA playback uses read-ahead readers, and corrected regions use the cached output. Offline playback waits for source reads. This preview is not an ARA host certification.

## AAX and ordinary non-ARA hosts

The AAX bundle is **unsigned**. Its compilation does not make it loadable in standard retail Pro Tools. Avid developer testing facilities or the official PACE signing/release process are needed. No Avid or PACE accounts, credentials or keys have been supplied or configured. See [Avid's AAX developer information](https://developer.avid.com/aax/).

This AAX target is Native, not HDX DSP, and does not provide ARA binding or an AudioSuite workflow. It shares the engine and editor. In a host without ARA or REAPER's native API:

1. Insert the effect on the target and route the primary microphone to its **Reference** sidechain.
2. Enable the reference bus, press Capture, and play continuously through the dialogue. Press **Stop capture** afterwards. The current capture limit is 30 seconds; seeking/looping during capture rejects the capture.
3. Analyze, then replay the same timeline to compare Original and Aligned. Apply keeps the corrected snapshot in plug-in state; Revert returns to normal input. Applied sidechain renders are stored in the host's plug-in state.

This is an offline capture-and-replay workflow, not continuous analysis of new incoming material. Recapture after editing the source performance, insert chain, gain or timing. Use the host's own transport where host transport control is unavailable. Each AAX instance handles its own target and reference; it does not enumerate Pro Tools project items or inherit REAPER-only APIs.

## Interface

The native vector logo and **Ebin Augustin** name are embedded. In REAPER, the interface reads the active theme colours and adjusts text contrast. Other hosts use the native default palette.

All captured tracks and clips appear in the waveform overview. Wheel zooms time, Shift-wheel pans time, Ctrl-wheel zooms lane height, and Alt-wheel pans enlarged lanes. Double-click or Fit restores the full overview. Scrollbars appear only after zooming their axes. Clicking/dragging waveforms moves the REAPER cursor; clicks select corresponding REAPER items, and Shift-drag updates REAPER's time selection. ARA uses its host playback-position request. Optional measured statistics, delay, spectrum, phase/coherence, correlation and comb views are selected under Views. Click a target waveform to choose its diagnostics. Display spectra sample eight blocks; the complete output receives processing.

The native port currently exposes Dynamic time and Time + phase. Legacy Lua-only options such as custom band/profile editing, sparse marker and track-offset correction modes, candidate editing, and export reports remain in the companion action. This native preview does not claim complete feature or host-behaviour parity with either that action or Auto-Align Post.

## Engine and build

The original 1.4.5 deterministic core and continuous/spectral processor are embedded in an internal Lua 5.4.8 runtime. Double-precision FFT and the matching 32-tap interpolation are implemented in C++; processing and diagnostics run off the audio callback. The audio callback plays immutable cached results; host API reads/edits stay on the message thread. Analysis resampling uses a windowed low-pass interpolator. The native routing, resampling and host wrappers are new code and require qualification beyond the original Lua test evidence.

Source is included with the release. Dependencies are JUCE 8.0.12, ARA SDK 2.2.0 and Lua 5.4.8. `deps/ARA_SDK/dependency-commits.json` pins the exact ARA API/library commits. JUCE includes the AAX SDK sources used for the unsigned build. The source distribution uses the open-source licensing options of these dependencies; preserve their notices and see LICENSES.

For source builds, install a Windows C++ toolchain and CMake 3.22+. Configure with `cmake -S . -B build -DJUCE_SOURCE_PATH=path/to/JUCE` from a suitable developer shell, then build the `DAE_VST3`, `DAE_AAX`, `dae_engine_tests`, `pc` and `dae_format_probe` targets. `prepare.py` regenerates the embedded processor from the companion Lua action; generated sources are already included. `fetch_ara.py` downloads the pinned public ARA release if needed. The build helper accepts explicit JUCE, compiler and Windows SDK paths.

Executed checks and remaining host validation are recorded in `VALIDATION.md`. No user REAPER or Pro Tools project was opened or modified by the native build checks.

# Native 2.0.0 preview validation — 10 November 2026

Built Windows x64 Release bundles with MSVC 14.44, Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0, CMake, JUCE 8.0.12, ARA SDK 2.2.0 and Lua 5.4.8. The original Lua action remains version 1.4.5.

Four CTest entries passed:

1. **Native engine:** complex FFT reconstruction, integer interpolation, a known 3 ms delay and corrected audio residual, a 1-to-4 ms delay change near the third second, measured before/after spectra and cancellation, finite spectral output, automatic polarity, silence rejection and cancellation. These are generated 16 kHz fixtures, not recorded dialogue or matched vendor benchmarks.
2. **Processor workflow:** a stereo target/reference capture, background analysis, Apply, replay residual, immediate audio playback from a restored state, resetting a previously applied state, Revert and a rendered native interface preview. The same executable uses mocked REAPER APIs to check accessor lifetime, source replacement, undo-block balance, preservation of current item/take colours and selection, explicit peak building, recognition of external Undo, stale-input refusal and rollback after a rejected source swap. Mock sources are confined to a generated workspace fixture directory.
3. **VST3/ARA registration:** loaded the actual VST3 binary and enumerated its audio-effect, controller and ARA main-factory classes. Instantiated its ARA entry interface and verified the factory ID, archive ID and document-controller creation callback. This verifies real binary/interface registration; it does not exercise a complete host-bound ARA document.
4. **AAX binary registration:** loaded the actual unsigned AAX binary and verified its ACF registration export. This is not a Pro Tools qualification or a signing check.

The native UI preview was visually inspected. It is drawn by the compiled editor using synthetic captured audio, not a graphic mockup. It shows the embedded vector logo/name, two captured tracks, controls and applied-state interface.
